summary.title: FIGARO: Controllable Music Generation Using Expert and Learned Features
summary.objective: To introduce a controllable symbolic music generative framework that achieves fine-grained and global control by generating multi-track, multi-time-signature symbolic music conditioned on high-level expert and learned features via description-to-sequence learning.
summary.problem: Controlling the output of modern symbolic music generative models to match user expectations remains difficult, as prior methods are mostly limited to single-track/single-time-signature music, prompt-based conditioning that gets forgotten, or lack human-interpretable and fine-grained temporal control.
summary.methodology: The authors introduce description-to-sequence learning, a self-supervised framework where high-level features (descriptions) are extracted partition-wise (bar-by-bar) and used to train a sequence-to-sequence model to reconstruct the original piece. They use REMI+, an extension of the REMI representation incorporating instruments, time signatures, and higher temporal resolution (12 sub-beats per quarter note). Conditioning features combine hand-crafted 'expert descriptions' (time signature, note density, mean pitch, mean velocity, mean duration, instruments, chords) and 'learned descriptions' from a bar-level VQ-VAE. Evaluation includes fluency (perplexity), fidelity metrics (F1-score for chords/instruments, time signature accuracy, Macro Overlapping Area, NRMSE, cosine similarity for chroma and grooving), out-of-distribution robustness (description splicing and mixing), and a pairwise listening study.
summary.architecture: A Transformer sequence-to-sequence model (4 encoder layers, 6 decoder layers, relative positional embeddings, bar and beat-position embeddings; 44.6M parameters) combined with a bar-level Transformer VQ-VAE (4 encoder, 6 decoder layers; 43.7M parameters with 16 latent codes and codebook size 2048).
summary.results: FIGARO outperforms prior baselines (Choi et al., 2020; MuseMorphose; unconditional Music Transformer) in multi-track symbolic style transfer, description fidelity, and fluency (achieving a perplexity of 1.705). It shows strong robustness against out-of-distribution conditions like bar splicing and mixing. In a subjective listening study with 691 participants and 7,569 comparisons, FIGARO won pairwise against each baseline with p < 10^-7 and achieved a 39.3% win rate against real human-composed music.
summary.limitations: The model is strictly conditional and requires creative description inputs rather than operating unconditionally. REMI+ cannot represent expressive timing/human performance nuances like continuous tempo drift and micro-offsets. The training data predominantly represents Western music.
summary.future_work: Training an unconditional prior model to generate descriptions automatically to reduce manual input; adding new conditioning functions such as melody control; and extending the description-to-sequence learning objective to other domains such as natural language story generation.
